subsections.heading: Update 3 — confirmed facts and reported details
paragraphs: AllThingsHow described Update 3 in its October 28 reporting. The article says more content and tools were added but does not offer a complete developer-signed itemized changelog; avoid inventing exact new weapon names.

sections.heading: Weapons vs Sandbox Gadgets: What Is Different?
sections.intro: The game is a physics sandbox; not every item belongs in a competitive fighting tier list.

subsections.heading: Map-dependent experiments
paragraphs: To compare results, try one tool on the same dummy and in the same environment before changing another factor. This is a testing method, not an assertion that a weapon has a fixed damage amount.

sections.heading: All Realistic Ragdoll Engine Badges
sections.intro: The Realistic Ragdoll Engine badges listed here are four names appearing in October 2026 game-specific references. A badge’s existence does not prove its unlock trigger. Start with the documented visit and fan clues before testing the others.

subsections.heading: Welcome — first visit
paragraphs: Published listings describe a visit or joining requirement. Join the No Knees! version of the game, not another similar Roblox experience.

For the simplest badge check, open the correct No Knees! experience, join it normally and inspect the badges area of your Roblox profile afterward. The Welcome name and public descriptions point to the visit itself. Do not purchase a game pass or move to a different ragdoll game to attempt this first-time task.

subsections.heading: Against the Wind — launch a dummy with the fan
paragraphs: A third-party game guide links this badge to launching a dummy with a fan. The map, fan location and exact condition have not been independently reproduced by this site.

If you are trying the fan challenge, locate a fan or air-launch interaction in the current map and observe whether your dummy is visibly propelled. After the attempt, check for a Roblox badge notification or ownership in your profile. The reported clue is “launch a dummy with the fan”; a specific map name, distance threshold or button sequence has not been independently verified.

sections.heading: Which Game Pass Is Right for You?
sections.intro: There is no substantiated universal “best” pass. Consider what you actually want to experiment with.

paragraphs: If you prefer map physics experiments, buying a themed tool bundle may offer little value. If you use a class of gadgets regularly, inspect its exact official pass perks first.

For a first-time player, the best comparison is not which pass costs the most. Start with the free physics sandbox and notice which tools or events you actually use. Then decide whether a named pass grants useful permanent access. If the official description does not clearly say what is included, skip the purchase rather than assuming an attractive label guarantees particular weapons.
